Started at the label $\mathsf{act0}$, with any value of its internal variable, on the stacks holding the code $c$, the clock $t$ and the configuration $k$, with $q'$ on the next-state stack, $s$ on the action stack and all other stacks empty, the program of the clocked universal machine reaches the label $\mathsf{fin}$, with some value of…
nodes.title: The tape update

nodes.summary: For a configuration $k$ with state $q$, head cell $h$, cells $\ell$ left of the head and cells $r$ right of the head (nearest first), a next state $q'$ and an action $s$, the step bound of the tape update is $q + q' + s + h + \ell_0 + r_0 + 8$, where $\ell_0$ and $r_0$ are the first entries of $\ell$ and $r$, taken to be $0$ for an empty list.
nodes.title: Step bound of the tape update

nodes.summary: A configuration $k$ is bounded by a natural number $M$ when its state, its head cell and every cell left and right of the head are at most $M$.
nodes.title: Configurations bounded by $M$

nodes.summary: The cell of a natural number $n$ is the list of bits consisting of $n$ copies of the bit true (units) followed by one bit false (a marker).
nodes.title: The cell of a number

nodes.summary: The cells of a list $(n_1, \ldots, n_m)$ of natural numbers are the concatenation of the cells of $n_1, \ldots, n_m$ in this order, so that the cell of $n_1$ comes first (on top of a stack).
nodes.title: The cells of a list of numbers

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and a clock $T$, let $|C|$ be the length of the code stack of $c$. The step bound of the clocked simulation on the clock $T$ is $T + 1$ times the cost of one round of the loop on configurations whose numbers are at most $|C| + 2$, that is, $(T + 1)(14|C| + 19)$.
nodes.title: Step bound of the clocked simulation

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code, $x$ a list of bits and $T$ a natural number, and let $|C|$ be the length of the code stack of $c$. Start the program of the clocked universal machine at the label $\mathsf{sc0}$, with any value of its internal variable, on the stacks holding the code $c$, the clock $T$ and the initial configuration on $x$, all other stacks empty. If the clocked evaluation of $c$ on $x$ for $T$ steps is defined,…
nodes.title: The clocked universal machine on stacks

nodes.summary: The code stack of a code $c$ is the list of bits formed by the cells of the numbers $q, a, q', s$ of every entry $(q, a, q', s)$ of $c$ (a table position $(q, a)$ holding the transition $(q', s)$), with the entries ordered by $q$ and then by $a$, and the four numbers of an entry in the order $q, a, q', s$.
nodes.title: The code stack

nodes.summary: The unit decoder sends the bit true (a unit) to the bit true, and sends the bit false (a marker) to no bit, which ends a block.
nodes.title: Decoding units

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T$, the input of the clocked universal machine is the list of bits formed by the cell of $T$, then the cells of the input word of $x$, then the cell of $0$ (a blank cell, the single bit false), then the code stack of $c$ in reverse order.
nodes.title: Input encoding of the clocked universal machine

nodes.summary: The output bits of an optional list of numbers: no result (a timeout) is encoded as the single bit false, and a result $l$ is encoded as the bit true followed by the cells of $l$, where a number $n$ is written as $n$ bits true followed by one bit false.
nodes.title: Output encoding of the clocked universal machine

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, the list of quadruples $(q, a, q', s)$, one for each state $q$ and symbol $a$ inside the table of $c$ whose table entry is a transition $(q', s)$ (enter the state $q'$ and do the action coded by $s$); halting positions are skipped. The quadruples are listed row by row, by increasing $q$, and within a row by increasing $a$.
nodes.title: Entries of a code

nodes.summary: The step budget for scanning past an entry $(q, a, q', s)$ of the code stack is $5q + 5a + 2q' + 2s + 30$.
nodes.title: Cost of scanning past one entry

nodes.summary: For a list of quadruples of natural numbers, the list of natural numbers obtained by replacing each quadruple $(q, a, q', s)$ by the four numbers $q, a, q', s$ in this order, keeping the order of the quadruples.
nodes.title: Numbers of a list of entries

nodes.summary: For every code $c$ and all natural numbers $q$ and $a$, looking up the key $(q, a)$ in the entries of $c$ gives the entry of the table of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$: the pair $(q', s)$ if that position holds the transition $(q', s)$, and no result if it halts, including every position outside the table.
nodes.title: Scanning the entries finds the table entry

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $a$ and a list of quadruples $(q_i, a_i, q'_i, s_i)$ of natural numbers, the result is the pair $(q'_i, s_i)$ of the first quadruple in the list with $q_i = q$ and $a_i = a$, and no result if no quadruple has the key $(q, a)$. This is the order in which the machine scans the code stack.
nodes.title: Looking up a key in a list of entries

nodes.summary: The clocked universal machine has fifteen stacks: the state $Q$, the next state $N$, the action $A$ and the head cell $H$ (these four hold counters of units), the cells left ($L$) and right ($R$) of the head, the code $C$, the scan buffer $B$, the scratch counters $T$, $U$, $V$, the clock $\mathrm{Ck}$, and the parsing stacks: the encoded input $X$, the parse buffer $P$ and the output $O$.

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and a number $M$, the loop step time is $10\ell + 4M + 11$, where $\ell$ is the length of the code stack of $c$. It serves as the cost bound of one round of the loop (a simulated step and a clock tick) on configurations whose numbers are at most $M$.

nodes.title: Reading the input

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a natural number $T$, let $w_1, \dots, w_n$ be the input word of $x$ (false as the symbol $1$, true as $2$), with $w_1$ read as $0$ when $x$ is empty, let $S_j = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (w_i + j)$, and let $m$ be the length of the code stack of $c$. The cost of reading the input is $T + 2 + (S_3 + 2) + (S_1 + 1) + (w_1 + 2) + (m + 1)$.

nodes.summary: The program of the clocked universal machine gives an instruction for every label. Numbers sit on stacks as counters of units (the bit true), and a cell is a counter followed by a marker (the bit false).

nodes.summary: For every code $c$, list of bits $x$ and clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the step bound of the whole clocked universal machine on $(c, x, T)$ is at most $18 (n + 1)^2$, where $n$ is the length of the input encoding of $(c, x, T)$.
nodes.title: The step bound of the clocked universal machine is quadratic

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a natural number $T$, the step bound of the whole machine on $(c, x, T)$ is the sum of three terms: the cost of reading the input on $(c, x, T)$, the step bound of the clocked simulation on the clock $T$, and the output bound $4\,(|x| + T + 1)\,(|C| + 3) + 8$, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$ and $|C|$ is the length of the code stack of $c$.

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
